translit:
|| Ath Shri Arjun Gita ||29||
Dhanraj-Adhyaruji Maharaj rachit

Shri guru pratape gaiye | kirpa te sadhu jan ||
Parbrahm maro atma | marun man te Arjun ||
Arjun suno gita sar | Pandav manjo nidhari ||tek||

Tyare Arjune em ja puchhyun | tamo sambhalo Vaikunthray ||
Ek sar gita kaho swami | nij bhaktno mahimay || Arjun ||1||

Tyare Shri Hari valtun ocharya | tamo Arjun dharjo man ||
Ek sar gita sambhale | avatar teno dhanya || Arjun ||2||

Chaud lok vash mahare | vali brahmand kero bhar ||
Te dhanya dhanya mara dasne | mane rakhe rude mojhar || Arjun ||3||

Jal madhye jem padma chhe | tene sparsh nahi re lagar ||
E chinh mara dasnun | jene valge na vishay vikar || Arjun ||4||

Sansarman sarso rahe | ne man mari pas ||
Mayaman lubdhe nahi | te jan maro das || Arjun ||5||

Muj bhakt te mujne bhaje | jene haiye het hamesh ||
To bhakt tene janiye | je kare na koino dvesh || Arjun ||6||

Ek mane mujne bhaje | antar ani dhruv ||
Bhakt tyare janiye | jivno te thay shiv || Arjun ||7||

Karman tulsi karne tulsi | kanthe tulsi har ||
Bahu tilak chhaya shobhatan | muj bhaktno shangar || Arjun ||8||

Mara bhaktne jane nahi | pakhand puje lok ||
Bahu dambh adambar kare | te janun sarve phok || Arjun ||9||

Uttam thai mune na bhaje | chandal kahie teh ||
Chandal thai mujne bhaje | te jan mari deh || Arjun ||10||

Mara bhaktne jane nahi | chandal kahie teh ||
Te mara bhakt kere karane | musal nikandu eh || Arjun ||11||

Hun Ishwar chhun jad jivno | mare nahi maran avatar ||
Chhatan bhakt kere karane | hun deh dharun chhun sar || Arjun ||12||

Muj bhakt kere karane | avatar lidha dash ||
Hun Niranjan Nirakar | te mane bhakte kidho vash || Arjun ||13||

Vali bhakt kere karane | hun gayo vasme van ||
Men Ravan mari rajya apyun | Vibhishan rajan || Arjun ||14||

Durvasa rushie dubhavyo | muj atma Ambarish ||
Bhay chakra meli chhediyo | men bhali lagadi shikh || Arjun ||15||

Balirayne men bandhiyo | devoni kidhi sar ||
Patal apyun rayne | tyan hun rahyo chhadidar || Arjun ||16||

Gokul vishe hun avataryo | sir pichh dharto mor ||
Khato hun makhan taskari | jugman kahevayo chor || Arjun ||17||

Vali Jashodae mane bandhiyo | hun jodi rahyo behu hath ||
Din thayo mara dasno | hun chaud bhuvanno nath || Arjun ||18||

Vali Indra jyare kopiyo | tyare koie na avyun ad ||
Men Gokul rakhyun reltun | Gopine ladavyan lad || Arjun ||19||

Vali solsen sahasman hun ramyo | maro koie na jane bhed ||
Mara bhakt kere karane | mune kahe lampat ved || Arjun ||20||

Viranchi vachharun hari gayo | te kari gayo ja adharm ||
Hun navan nipjavi laviyo | maro koie na jane marm || Arjun ||21||

Tahan Kanse mujne marvane | mokalya daitya apar ||
Men tehne sanharine | Vrajni kidhi sar || Arjun ||22||

Mamane hun malva gayo | tyan mali Kubja nar ||
Thodak chandan karane | men apyun rup apar || Arjun ||23||

Vali pratham pole pesatan | pariyate didhi gal ||
Men marine vastar lidha | sohaviya goval || Arjun ||24||

Vali tyanthi agal chaltan | malan lavi har ||
Men arth sadhyo ehno | apya padarath char || Arjun ||25||

Vali margman napik malyo | men apyun darpan hath ||
Purna manorath te tana | men rakhyo mari sath || Arjun ||26||

Sambandhi te janne hane | chandalno te ansh ||
Mara bhakt kere karane | men maryo mamo Kans || Arjun ||27||

Men Sudamane santoshiyo | ek kangna kanne kaj ||
Sampat api tehne | nav nidh sidh ath || Arjun ||28||

Ek var Vidur gher jai | arogya bhaji pan ||
Men lad padyan mara dasna | rayna modyan man || Arjun ||29||

Pachhi Kaurav kul sanghariyun | men saryo taro arth ||
Hun chaud bhuvanno rajiyo | men hankyo taro rath || Arjun ||30||

Ek var to hun vanman gayo | tahan van disatan ghanghor ||
Men bhav joyo bhiladino | juthan te prasyan bor || Arjun ||31||

Ame ghanan mali govaliya | ramta te gaya maha van ||
Bahu bhav joi rushi narno | ame jachi te lidhan ann || Arjun ||32||

Prahlad pitae parabhavyo | men khambh mahi puryo vas ||
Dusht daitya vidariyo | men rude rakhyo das ||33||

Vali Dhruvne dukh pamadyo | ne kadhyo vanvas ||
Te balake mane vash karyo | dhan dhan maro das || Arjun ||34||

Chandrahasne Harishchandra raja | bhakt mara teh ||
Pade vipat na visare | muj mugatna mani eh || Arjun ||35||

Jyare Sudhanvane lai nakhiyo | tate tel balti jhal ||
Mara dasne vela padi | tyare turat kari sambhal || Arjun ||36||

Draupadi kera patful kadhyan | hun pas nahi te kal ||
Mara bhaktne vela padi | turat kari sambhal || Arjun ||37||

Panchaline jyare parabhavi | pase te huta panch vir ||
Mara bhaktne men puriyan | navsen nevanun chir || Arjun ||38||

Ek kolie kautak karyun | ane lidhun marun rup ||
Rayni kanya parabhavi | par dal kopya bhup || Arjun ||39||

Men tyan jaine shun karyun | marun tej mukyun may ||
Pardalno parajay karyo | marun birad padyun tyay || Arjun ||40||

Ajamil maha pataki | mamki gunika jeh ||
Je smaran kartan maharun | Vaikunth pohoti teh || Arjun ||41||

Gajrajne grahe grahyo | tyan lidhun marun nam ||
Em ek kartan behunan | men kidhan tehnan kam || Arjun ||42||

Hun man ne mara bhaktman | antar na hoy lagar ||
Muj bhaktne olakhe nahi | te bhuli bhame sansar || Arjun ||43||

Mahara bhakt dukhiye hun dukhi | sukhiye te sukhiyo jan ||
Mahara bhaktne jo dubhave | te mane mare ban || Arjun ||44||

Swarg mrutyu patalman | jal thal maharo vas ||
Tatva kahun hun tujne | hun thaki adko das || Arjun ||45||

Jap yagno nahi malun | nahi tap tirath ke dan ||
Arjun mahima janjo | marun bhaktithi chhe gyan || Arjun ||46||

Hun bhaktni sange pharun | mane bhaktno adhar ||
Arjun mahima janjo | kaheta na ave par || Arjun ||47||

Hari bhakt mahima suni | Arjun pamya harakh apar ||
Murchhit thai avani padyo | netre vahe jaldhar || Arjun ||48||

A gitane je anubhave | je gay nar ne nar ||
Arjun evun janjo | te pame pad nirdhar || Arjun ||49||

E bhakt mahima maharo | kone kalyo nav jay ||
Jenun bhagya hoy te anubhave | Dhandas gita gay || Arjun ||50||

|| Iti Shri Arjun (Dhandas) gita sampurna ||29||
translation:
|| Here begins the Shri Arjun Gita ||29|| - composed by Dhanraj-Adhyaruji Maharaj

Opening refrain (tek): By the grace of Shri Guru let us sing, by the mercy of the sadhu-folk. Parbrahm (the Supreme Reality) is my very soul; my mind is Arjun. Arjun, listen to the essence of the Gita; O Pandav, hold it as certain.

1. Then Arjun asked this: "Listen, O Lord of Vaikunth. Tell me, master, the one essential Gita - the greatness of your own devotee."
2. Then Shri Hari answered: "Arjun, set your mind upon this. Whoever listens to this one essential Gita - blessed is his birth."
3. The fourteen worlds are under my sway, and the burden of the whole universe is mine as well; yet blessed, blessed is that servant of mine who keeps me within his heart.
4. As the lotus stands in the midst of water and the water does not touch it in the least - that is the mark of my servant: no craving or corruption clings to him.
5. He lives fully in the world, yet his mind stays close to me; he is not caught by greed for maya (illusion) - know him to be my servant.
6. He is my devotee who worships me with love always in his heart; know that one to be a devotee who bears hatred toward no one.
7. He who worships me with a single mind, holding steadfastness (dhruv) within - know him then to be a devotee: his jiv (individual soul) becomes Shiv.
8. Tulsi in the hand, tulsi at the ear, a tulsi garland at the throat, many tilak marks shining upon him - that is my devotee's ornament.
9. Those who do not recognise my devotee, and worship shams instead; who make a great show of hypocrisy and pomp - all of that I count as empty.
10. He who, though highborn, does not worship me - call him an outcaste; he who, though an outcaste, worships me - know him to be my own body.
11. He who does not recognise my devotee - call him an outcaste; for my devotee's sake I uproot such a one, wiping out his very family line.
12. I am the Lord of every inert creature; for me there is neither death nor birth - yet for my devotee's sake I truly take on a body.
13. For my devotee's sake I took the ten avatars (incarnations); I am Niranjan, the stainless Formless One, yet the devotee has brought me under his sway.
14. Again, for my devotee's sake I went into the harsh forest; I killed Ravan and gave away the kingdom, making Vibhishan king.
15. When the sage Durvasa wronged Ambarish, who is my own soul, I loosed the dreaded chakra (discus) and cut him down - I taught him a good lesson.
16. I bound King Bali and looked after the gods; I gave the netherworld to that king, and there I myself stayed on as his doorkeeper.
17. I was born in Gokul, wearing a peacock feather on my head; I ate butter by stealth, and in the world I was called a thief.
18. Jashoda too bound me, and I stood there with both hands joined - I, the lord of the fourteen worlds, became humble before my own servant.
19. Again, when Indra raged, no one came forward to stand in the way; I kept Gokul from being washed away, and fondly indulged the gopis.
20. Again, I sported among the sixteen thousand (solsen sahas) - no one knows my secret; for my devotee's sake the Veda calls me a libertine.
21. Virinchi (Brahma) carried off the calves - in doing so he did an unrighteous thing; I made new ones and brought them back, and no one knows my mystery.
22. There Kans sent countless demons to kill me; I destroyed them and took care of Vraj.
23. I went to meet my maternal uncle, and there the hunchbacked woman Kubja met me; for a little sandal-paste I gave her boundless beauty.
24. Again, as I entered the first gate, the washerman abused me; I struck him down and took the clothes, and adorned the cowherds with them.
25. Going on further from there, the flower-woman brought a garland; I fulfilled her purpose and gave her the four padarath (the four great gains of life).
26. Again, on the road a barber met me; I placed a mirror in his hand; his longing being fulfilled, I kept him with me.
27. One who kills his own kinsman is a portion of an outcaste; yet for my devotee's sake I killed my uncle Kans.
28. I satisfied Sudama for the sake of a single grain of parched millet; I gave him wealth - the nine treasures and the eight siddhis (powers).
29. Once I went to Vidur's house and ate the leaves of a plain pot-herb; I indulged my servant fondly and broke the pride of kings.
30. Then the Kaurav clan was destroyed and I accomplished your purpose; I who am king of the fourteen worlds drove your chariot.
31. Once I went into the forest, and there the woods looked dark and dense; I saw the Bhil woman's devotion, and ate the berries she had already tasted.
32. Many of us cowherds together went playing into the great forest; seeing the deep devotion of the sages' wives, we begged and took food from them.
33. When Prahlad was tormented by his father, I filled the pillar with my presence; I tore the wicked demon apart, and kept my servant in my heart.
34. Again, when Dhruv was given pain and driven out into the forest, that child brought me under his power - blessed, blessed is my servant.
35. Chandrahas and King Harishchandra - they are devotees of mine; when calamity falls they do not forget me: these are the jewels of my crown.
36. When Sudhanva was picked up and thrown by his father into oil blazing in flames, my servant's hour of trial came, and at once I took care of him.
37. When Draupadi's garment was pulled away, I was not near her at that moment; my devotee's hour of trial came, and at once I took care of her.
38. When Panchali was dishonoured, her five heroes were standing right beside her; for my devotee I supplied nine hundred and ninety-nine lengths of cloth.
39. A Koli man played a trick and took on my form; he dishonoured the king's daughter, and the enemy host and its king were enraged.
40. What did I do when I went there? I placed my own splendour within him; I defeated the enemy host, and established my good name there.
41. Ajamil was a great sinner, and so was that ganika (courtesan) who was mine; merely by remembering my name, she reached Vaikunth.
42. When the crocodile seized the king of elephants, there he uttered my name; thus by doing one deed I accomplished the purpose of both of them.
43. Between me and my devotee there is not the least distance; whoever does not recognise my devotee wanders lost through the world.
44. When my devotee grieves I grieve; when he is happy, know that I am happy; whoever wounds my devotee shoots an arrow into me.
45. In heaven, on earth and in the netherworld, in the waters and on the land is my dwelling; I tell you the truth of it: my servant is greater than I am.
46. I am not to be reached by muttered prayer or sacrifices, nor by austerity, pilgrimage or charity; Arjun, know this greatness: knowledge of me comes through bhakti (devotion).
47. I move about in the company of my devotee; the devotee is my support; Arjun, know this greatness - it cannot be told to the end.
48. Hearing the greatness of Hari's devotees, Arjun was filled with boundless joy; he fainted and fell to the ground, streams of water flowing from his eyes.
49. Whoever experiences this Gita, whatever man or woman sings it - Arjun, know this: he surely attains that state.
50. This greatness of my devotee is my own, and no one can fathom it; he whose fortune it is, experiences it - Dhandas sings this Gita.

|| Here ends the Shri Arjun (Dhandas) Gita, complete ||29||
